1726015.title: Cartografía

1726143.title: Only Good Feelings

1729663.title: September Afternoon
1729663.overview: A couple refuses to accept that summer is over. For a last time, they head to the coast with the intention of spending two afternoons together between sand dunes and sea water. The temperatures have long been too cold for sandals and shorts; the blustery autumn wind is no substitute for cosy rays of summer sun. On the way to the beach, they cross paths with a woman they know loosely. Upon arrival, they look in vain for a dune to take shelter from the wind; a small dam is built and defended hard against the tide, an attempt to erect a windbreak is made. These desperate struggles against the encroaching elements are merely a brief interlude before the situation unravels into a disaster of an entirely different magnitude. A contemporary cosmic catastrophe.

1732479.title: 14th

1751231.title: Act 3
1751231.overview: The latest in Christine Molloy and Joe Lawlor’s series of cinematic essays is a rich and thought- provoking journey through aging, legacy and the intersection between artistic and personal relationships. Molloy and Lawlor engage in a witty and moving conversation that explores family history and their latest project, a film about groundbreaking artists Claude Cahun and Marcel Moore. As they analyse this decades-long relationship, they identify parallels between these two artists and their own lives. Act 3 celebrates the power of connection, of artistic exploration and the importance of memory to shape our present and future.

1753791.title: Curriculum Vitae
1753791.overview: During a tense job interview, Manuel desperately needs to secure the position, forcing him to confront his past.

1754879.title: The Cord
1754879.overview: Kuanysh, who is about to enroll at an American university, is the pride of his single mother, Dinara. Divorced when Kuanysh was young, Dinara has devoted herself to caring for her son, but as a teenager he has a world his mother is not privy to. One day, Kuanysh goes to a club with his friends and becomes involved in an assault incident, which turns into a homicide when the victim dies during the investigation. The wealthy and influential parents of Kuanysh’s friends attempt to make him the culprit, and now Dinara must protect her son by her own means.

1756159.title: Silent Mode

This documentary is a road movie in which performance, the body, and poetry fuel a journey that begins at the river’s source and flows out to the open sea, moving between the arid landscape and the ocean, between devastation and what endures.

1757503.title: Where is Ava?
1757503.overview: To protect themselves from a mysterious virus that turns women into men, a family retreats to an alpine chalet. Their desire to preserve the female sex within the family leads them down a path of radicalization. The descent into inhumanity unfolds almost imperceptibly, and patterns of behavior long thought to be outgrown resurface. Better able to cope with protogyny, the children offer a small glimmer of hope.

1767679.title: Under My Skin
1767679.overview: The evening Gabriel celebrates his abuser’s conviction, he is met with Lucien’s tenderness.

1768383.title: Agia
1768383.overview: In the 1990s, Albania's totalitarian regime is coming to an end. Agia, a young woman in a remote village still ruled by rigid codes of honour and silence, is barred from learning her family's craft. In her first act of defiance, she secretly begins mastering the tradition reserved for men. When this plunges her into a wider world, Agia dares to assert not only work and visibility, but also her own desires. Her belated coming of age becomes a quiet rebellion, mirroring that of a nation struggling to redefine itself.

1769279.title: Keep
1769279.overview: As debt collectors close in, a young boy steals what's left of his home.

1770559.title: Abductees

1772415.title: Recording
1772415.overview: Doing as they are told by their parents, young girls swear in front of a top university that someday they will be admitted to it. Through a child’s perspective, home videos that presumably remain in the memories of mothers and fathers wishing for their children’s happiness are ironically transformed into an archive revealing the egotism of parents and the social structures that lie behind it. Stitched together out of home videos from the filmmaker’s own childhood, is this film a black comedy or a child’s small act of revenge?

1775231.title: feeling together
1775231.overview: Roars and shrieks sound in the dark. The camera turns to a man and woman ferociously cursing and hitting each other. The disturbance seems likely to grow and draw in the surrounding people in the village, but eventually the man and woman arguing break out in song, and their rage spreads into a group dance. Through a powerful single shot, this documentary poses questions about the relationships that bind the person who films, the people who are filmed, and the people who watch, that is, the audience.
